## Video 1 — color_picker

**What is visible**

- **Website surface:** The video opens on D&D Beyond’s own loading screen, navigation, promotional banner, and “Your Privacy Choices” cookie panel. The character sheet for Corvo Saggio then renders with D&D Beyond’s artwork, statistics, tabs, and red section outlines.
- **Extension surface:** Around 29 seconds, the extension’s dark, gold-accented control panel and separate **LAYER MANAGEMENT** panel appear. The sheet is enhanced with a decorative character frame and extension-styled borders.
- **Extension interaction:** A **SELECT DECORATIVE SHAPE** modal opens. It contains `BORDERS`, `SHAPES`, and `CUSTOM` tabs, category filters, decorative thumbnails, **Cancel**, and **Add Shape**. A decorative shape is selected and added; a **“Shape added”** toast appears. The shape count in Layer Management changes from one to two.
- This is a decorative-shape workflow, not a color-picker workflow.

**Layer 1 — asserted behavior**

- Control panel exposes **Color Picker** and filter controls: **NOT-VISIBLE**.
- Color Picker opens a 2D grid with swatches, greyscale, and **Continue**: **NOT-VISIBLE**.
- Choosing a swatch previews the hue and **Continue** closes the picker: **NOT-VISIBLE**.
- **Reset All Filters** restores default filter values: **NOT-VISIBLE**.

**Layer 2 — product-aim conformance**

- Working: the extension UI is clearly distinguishable through its dark “codex/workbench” styling and gold accents; the sheet decoration is visibly distinct from D&D Beyond’s base layout; the shape picker has clear tabs, filters, thumbnails, **Cancel**, and **Add Shape**; the **“Shape added”** toast provides useful confirmation.
- Missing/rough: no loading or transition affordance is visible between the plain sheet and the enhanced result—the enhancement and both panels appear abruptly. No first-run hint card is visible. The color/filter surface named by the suite is not shown in the recorded segment.

---

## Video 2 — manual_verification_phase2

**What is visible**

- **Website surface:** D&D Beyond loads, displays its own cookie banner and character-sheet content, then removes the cookie overlay.
- **Extension surface:** The extension adds its floating control panel, enhanced borders, decorative artwork, and Layer Management panel.
- **Extension interaction:** The control panel is shown with **LAYOUT** and **OUTPUT** sections. Visible actions include **Load**, **Reset to Default**, **Manage Clones**, **Add Shape**, **Manage Compact**, **AI Arrange**, **AI Settings**, **PRINT**, **Print settings**, and **Save to Browser**. A notice states **“No saved layout yet — the default template is loaded.”**
- The panel is later scrolled so **PROPERTIES** becomes visible.
- No first-run walkthrough appears.

**Layer 1 — asserted behavior**

- The four-step discoverability walkthrough behaves as documented: **NOT-VISIBLE**.
- No individual step, step indicator, next/back navigation, or walkthrough completion state is sampled.

**Layer 2 — product-aim conformance**

- Working: the extension is visually distinct from the base website; grouped sections make layout, output, and properties discoverable; the “no saved layout yet” notice explains why no saved template is active; the panel provides many clearly labeled actions.
- Missing/rough: the required first-run discovery experience is not shown. No activation loading overlay is visible; the extension panels and enhancements appear suddenly. The control panel is tall and dense, and some controls are small and low-contrast. No explanatory first-run card is observed.

---

## Video 3 — shape_layer_management

**What is visible**

- **Website surface:** The base D&D Beyond sheet loads behind D&D Beyond’s own cookie panel and spinner.
- **Extension surface:** The enhanced sheet appears with the extension’s dark control panel and Layer Management panel.
- **Extension interaction:** **Add Shape** opens the extension’s **SELECT DECORATIVE SHAPE** picker. The picker switches to the **SHAPES** tab, displays shape thumbnails, allows one to be selected, and then closes after **Add Shape**. A **“Shape added”** toast appears.
- Layer Management shows a dedicated **SHAPES** subsection, shape thumbnails, print/visibility/edit-style controls, and an **Add Shape** action. The count changes from one shape to two.

**Layer 1 — asserted behavior**

- Shapes live in a dedicated default shape-layer container: **VISIBLE** — Layer Management has a dedicated **SHAPES** section and shape entries.
- **Add new Layer** creates a second shape-layer container that becomes active: **NOT-VISIBLE** — no **Add new Layer** action or second layer container is shown.
- Adding a shape while the new layer is active places it into that layer: **NOT-VISIBLE** — a shape is added, but no newly created/active layer is demonstrated.
- Shape-layer rows provide per-layer Print/Visibility/Edit controls: **VISIBLE** — compact per-row controls are visible in the Shapes section, though their individual labels/icons are small.

**Layer 2 — product-aim conformance**

- Working: the decorative-shape picker is clearly extension-owned and stylistically distinct; the tabbed picker, filters, thumbnails, **Cancel**, and **Add Shape** are understandable; the **“Shape added”** toast confirms completion; shape management is clearly separated from ordinary sheet sections.
- Missing/rough: the core “new shape layer becomes active” workflow is not shown. No loading/transition overlay appears before the enhanced state. The per-row icons are visually small and lack obvious text labels on camera, which makes their exact Print/Visibility/Edit meanings less immediately discoverable.

---

## Video 4 — byok_settings_storage

**What is visible**

- **Website surface:** D&D Beyond loads its own cookie banner and character sheet.
- **Extension surface:** The extension’s control panel, Layer Management panel, sheet decoration, and borders appear.
- **Extension interaction:** An extension-styled **AI LAYOUT SETTINGS** modal opens. It exposes provider, model, a **Compatible base URL** field, explanatory text, a key-related section, and **Reveal**, **Remove key**, **Cancel**, and **Save** actions.
- The base URL is edited to a non-HTTPS value. The dialog then displays **“The base URL must be https.”** in red, and the base URL field receives a red invalid border. This is a working validation/error state.

**Layer 1 — asserted behavior**

- `js/ai_settings.js` is injected and the real permission set matches the specification: **NOT-VISIBLE**.
- The real BYOK dialog is the shared shell, masked at first paint, and non-alarming: **NOT-VISIBLE** — the shown dialog is AI layout configuration, not a demonstrably masked BYOK credential dialog.
- Reveal masks/unmasks without revealing a stored value: **NOT-VISIBLE**.
- A successful save persists, clears the field, and leaves nothing invalid: **NOT-VISIBLE**.
- A rejected base URL marks the **BASE** field rather than the first input: **VISIBLE** for the AI layout base URL—the base URL field itself is marked, not another field.
- The credential stays out of the layout record and host storage: **NOT-VISIBLE**.
- The store is invisible to the page world: **NOT-VISIBLE**.
- A typed key is not recorded: **NOT-VISIBLE**.
- After successful save, no credential-shaped content remains in the shared DOM: **NOT-VISIBLE**.

**Layer 2 — product-aim conformance**

- Working: the modal is clearly extension-owned; field-level validation is visible and targets the correct base URL field; the error text is specific; destructive/key controls are separated from normal settings; the extension remains clearly distinguishable from D&D Beyond’s UI.
- Missing/rough: the shown AI Layout Settings dialog does not visibly provide a complete BYOK credential reveal/save flow, so the core credential guarantees cannot be reviewed on camera. There is no activation transition overlay. The long explanatory copy is dense at the captured size, and the disabled/error treatment of the bottom action buttons is not consistently clear.

---

## Video 5 — settings_export_import

**What is visible**

- **Website surface:** D&D Beyond’s loading sequence, cookie banner, and plain character sheet are shown.
- **Extension surface:** The extension adds its control panel, Layer Management panel, decorative frame, and enhanced borders.
- The **OUTPUT** section of the control panel exposes both **Export Settings** and **Import Settings**.
- A notice says **“No saved layout yet — the default template is loaded.”**
- No export or import interaction is completed on camera.

**Layer 1 — asserted behavior**

- Control panel exposes **Export Settings** and **Import Settings**: **VISIBLE**.
- Export Settings downloads a JSON settings file: **NOT-VISIBLE**.
- Exported bundle carries every required customization type: **NOT-VISIBLE**.
- `validateSettingsBundle` rejects a malformed bundle by name and accepts a real one: **NOT-VISIBLE**.
- Import merges filters and AI settings without wiping reuse libraries: **NOT-VISIBLE**.
- Export → mutate → import restores exported values: **NOT-VISIBLE**.

**Layer 2 — product-aim conformance**

- Working: Export/Import are clearly exposed in a logical Output group; the extension’s visual identity remains clear; the “no saved layout” notice supplies useful state context.
- Missing/rough: no export confirmation, downloaded filename, JSON contents, import validation feedback, merge result, or persistence confirmation is shown. No loading/transition affordance appears during activation. The panel’s small type and dense vertical layout reduce readability.

---

## Video 6 — quick_switch_print

**What is visible**

- **Website surface:** D&D Beyond’s own loading UI, cookie panel, character sheet, and character artwork.
- **Extension surface:** The extension enhances the sheet and presents the dark control panel and Layer Management panel.
- The extension panel contains print-related actions such as **PRINT**, **Print settings**, and **Save to Browser**, and the Layer Management panel contains Print/Visibility-style controls for sections and shapes.
- No shape asset is switched, no print preview is opened, and no printed output is shown.

**Layer 1 — asserted behavior**

- **Switch Shape Asset** opens the picker pre-filtered to **Shapes**: **NOT-VISIBLE**.
- Switching a shape’s asset preserves its transform and updates the path: **NOT-VISIBLE**.
- Print CSS makes shapes fully opaque and hides UI chrome: **NOT-VISIBLE**.

**Layer 2 — product-aim conformance**

- Working: print-related controls are exposed; the extension is clearly distinguishable from the base site; the Layer Management panel provides per-item print controls.
- Missing/rough: the central asset-switching and print-output behaviors are not shown. There is no print preview, print-state transition, confirmation that chrome is hidden, or visible opacity comparison. No loading/transition affordance appears during activation.

---

## Video 7 — release_1_4_0

**What is visible**

- **Website surface:** The base D&D Beyond character sheet, its loading spinner, promotional banner, cookie dialog, and character artwork.
- **Extension surface:** The extension adds the control panel, Layer Management panel, red/gold sheet borders, a decorative frame, and a selectable **DEFENSES** section.
- The control panel exposes layout, output, and properties groups, including **Add Shape** and print/export-related actions.
- Layer Management reports **SECTIONS (22)** and **SHAPES (1)** and shows per-section and per-shape controls.

**Layer 1 — asserted behavior**

- Extension boots cleanly and the character sheet stays visible: **VISIBLE** — after the base site loads, the enhanced sheet remains visible and usable-looking.
- Control panel shows the **1.4.0 headline actions**: **PARTIALLY VISIBLE / NOT FULLY VERIFIABLE** — major actions such as **Add Shape**, **PRINT**, **Export Settings**, **Import Settings**, and related controls are visible, but no explicit version label or complete enumeration of the asserted headline-action set is shown.
- The 1.4.0 decoration/layer surfaces are present: **VISIBLE** — decorative frame/shape tooling and the Layer Management panel are present.

**Layer 2 — product-aim conformance**

- Working: the release surface is coherent and distinguishable; extension decorations and layer surfaces coexist with the sheet; the panel’s hierarchy is apparent.
- Missing/rough: no explicit **1.4.0** version identifier is visible in the sampled frames, so the release branding itself is not established. There is no activation loading overlay; the enhancement appears abruptly. No detailed first-run or release-tour affordance is visible.

---

## Video 8 — dom_refactor_guarantees

**What is visible**

- **Website surface:** D&D Beyond’s own loader, navigation, cookie banner, and character sheet appear first.
- **Extension surface:** The sheet becomes a set of wrapped, red-bordered extension sections. The extension’s control panel and Layer Management panel overlay the sheet. A decorative frame and character portrait are applied.
- The actions tab remains visible, but no spells-tab filtering, modal opening, or spell-row Details interaction is sampled.

**Layer 1 — asserted behavior**

- Sheet enhances with wrapped sections after selector migration: **VISIBLE** — the character sheet is divided into extension-wrapped, bordered boxes.
- Live **Spells** node keeps its tab filter interactive: **NOT-VISIBLE** — the Spells tab is visible, but no filter interaction is shown.
- Modal UI remains usable above the cleaned layout and sidebar portal is not hidden: **NOT-VISIBLE**.
- Spell rows expose extension **Details** triggers: **NOT-VISIBLE**.

**Layer 2 — product-aim conformance**

- Working: the extension’s wrapping and border treatment is visibly distinct from D&D Beyond’s original presentation; the sheet content remains readable; the floating panels coexist with the transformed layout.
- Missing/rough: the key interaction guarantees are not demonstrated: no live tab filtering, no modal-above-layout test, and no Details trigger. The enhancement appears without a loading/transition overlay. The large control and layer panels occupy substantial screen area, which could make the wrapped sheet harder to use on smaller displays.

## Overall assessment

- The extension’s own UI and sheet enhancements are visibly distinct from D&D Beyond’s website.
- Working affordances observed include the dark codex-style panels, the Layer Management surface, the decorative shape picker, selection/disabled states, the **“Shape added”** toast, the “no saved layout” notice, and field-level URL validation.
- Across the videos, **no smooth activation/loading transition is visible**; the enhanced state appears abruptly. The first-run discoverability walkthrough is also not witnessed.
- Several asserted behaviors are either absent from the sampled frames or only represented by static UI rather than exercised interactions.
